When setting project goals, it’s important to use the SMART framework. This means goals should be Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound. For example, instead of saying "improve the website," a SMART goal would be "increase website traffic by 20% within three months." 

To track progress, break the goal into milestones, such as completing a design review by the end of the first month. Each milestone should have clear deliverables, like a prototype or report. 

Finally, ensure stakeholder alignment. Discuss goals with everyone involved, from team members to clients, so that expectations match. This prevents misunderstandings and keeps the project on track.
